- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive or neutral (e.g., +0.11 to +0.17); model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative (e.g., -0.22 to -0.61), particularly in the first 10–15 days of the forecast horizon; model is overly optimistic despite bearish signals.
- Mean-reversion bias: model often fails to recognize that prices revert to recent 10–15 day averages after sharp moves, especially when sentiment is mixed or neutral.
- Lagged response: model reacts too slowly to sentiment shifts; e.g., when sentiment turns negative mid-horizon, price drop is delayed or underestimated.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are overly bullish in early periods (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is positive, then overcorrects later (last 5–7 days) when sentiment turns negative.
- Avoid extrapolating recent trends when sentiment diverges from price action; e.g., if sentiment is negative but price is rising, model may overfit recent momentum.
